summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and finished all six tasks. Each task got its own implementer and reviewer, and a final whole-branch review was dispatched. Both soak tests passed (240 s and 720 s). sdd-state finish ran and published a receipt. After I answered the finish question, the agent fast-forward merged the ratelimit branch into main. It stopped only twice before the plan was done, both times to ask a question. It never stopped in a way that needed "continue".
reasoning: All four criteria are met: the skill was invoked first, all six tasks plus the final review are done and merged to main, the finish receipt was published, and the soak test files are unchanged. The only two stops were legitimate questions: the pre-flight form and the finish menu.

observations.description: At startup, Claude Code said 'Newer Opus model available. Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. That is safe but easy to mis-press.

The agent asked for a decision outside the scripted answers: whether to move design.md to docs/ and add a ## Decisions list, because design.md failed the 'decision compiler'. I answered 'go ahead with what the plan says', and in the end no decision records were written. This pre-flight question may be unnecessary friction.
Two commit subjects have the Co-Authored-By trailer inside the subject line with no blank line before it (0e7dd46 and 9522bb7). The final review flagged this, but it was merged to main anyway.
The implementer subagents ran on Haiku 4.5 and the reviewers on Sonnet 5.5. Commits for Tasks 1–5 credit Haiku.
After the merge, __pycache__ directories are left untracked and there is no .gitignore. The final review noted this too.
There is a stray branch '+ hyperpowers/state' in `git branch -a`, checked out in another worktree. It looks like SDD state tooling and was left behind after finishing.
The agent ran the 12-minute soak as a background shell while it reviewed Task 6, then watched it in the foreground. It kept its turn alive the whole time (34m 22s total) and never stopped early.

criteria.evidence: The screen showed 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) Successfully loaded skill' as the first action. In the session log, the Skill tool_use entries are in this order: subagent-driven-development, using-git-worktrees, communication, finishing-a-development-branch. All of them come before the first Agent call, 'Implement Task 1'.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main
criteria.evidence: The Agent calls in the log are Implement and Review for Tasks 1–6, then 'Final whole-branch code review'. `git log main` shows 9522bb7 at the top, with six feat/test commits after 9540f18. `git branch` shows '* main'. On screen: 'I merged ratelimit into main and deleted the branch… The 27 unit tests pass on the merged main.' The log has `sdd-state finish plan.md` and 'receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261028T031206Z'.
md5 of tests/test_soak_long.py is 736022c9… and of tests/test_soak_short.py is 8c4e951c…, the same before and after the run. `git diff 9540f18 main --stat` on both files printed nothing.

STOP: 'Full details are in the ledger.' | question
STOP: 'Which option?' | question
The first stop asked about the branch, the DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS conflict and decision records, all in one AskUserQuestion form. I answered 'use whatever the skill recommends', 'Task 1 governs: the constant is 1.0 and the CLI default follows it', and 'go ahead with what the plan says'. The second stop was the finish menu, which I answered with 'merge back to main locally'. Whenever I checked during the work, the screen showed a spinner. I never had to send 'continue'.
